clue.text: Why, originally, a trendy northerner collected fine oak

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word Why only

parts.note: something trendy is in, fashionable
a Scot comes from the north of Britain

explanation.surface: Someone asks why a fashionable man from the north gathered up some good timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collected' is a link word here. Wainscot is high-grade oak boarding imported for panelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Wainscot is the name for top-quality oak timber, as used for wall panelling.

clue.text: Scout around once for one of Mowgli's brothers

definitions.meaning: the old name for a junior Scout, used formerly
in Kipling's Jungle Book, Mowgli is raised alongside young wolves

explanation.definitionFit: Junior Scouts were once called by this name, borrowed from Kipling, where the wolf pack's young are Mowgli's siblings.

clue.text: Drinking-place knight installed in home

indicators.note: installed in says the knight goes inside the word for home

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A knight has been put up at a house where drinks are served.
explanation.definitionFit: An inn is a pub, a place for drinking.

clue.text: Way single mother with child becomes builder

parts.note: St is an abbreviation for street, a way
single means one
ma is mother
a son is a child

explanation.surface: A single mother and her child find their way into the building trade.
explanation.definitionFit: A stonemason builds and works in stone, so is a kind of builder.

clue.text: Utter hatred for Roman theatre

indicators.note: utter means say aloud, indicating a word heard rather than written

parts.note: odium is hatred or loathing

explanation.surface: Total loathing for an ancient Roman playhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utter' reads as the adjective 'complete' but is the verb, a sound signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An odeum was a roofed theatre in ancient Rome or Greece for music and recitals.

clue.text: One who digs empty prattle

definitions.meaning: someone who digs or pokes at another, that is, one who jabs

explanation.definitionFit: A person who jabs is literally a jabber; as a noun the word also means gabbled nonsense talk.

clue.text: Roguish maiden excluded from demonstration

indicators.note: excluded from says the maiden letter is taken out

parts.note: a protest march is a demonstration
M stands for maiden, a cricket term for an over without runs

explanation.surface: A mischievous young woman is barred from a protest.
explanation.definitionFit: Arch means playfully mischievous, a synonym of roguish.

clue.text: Conductor turns tail, finding badly rent creature in tree

indicators.note: turns tail says the conductor's name has its last two letters swapped round

parts.note: Sir Thomas Beecham, the famous English conductor

indicators.note: badly signals the word rent is jumbled

explanation.surface: A conductor flees and finds an animal that has been torn in a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns tail' swaps the final AM of BEECHAM to give BEECHMA; 'badly' turns RENT into RTEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The beech marten is a European weasel-like animal that lives in woodland and climbs trees.

clue.text: Answer referring to singular body of water

parts.note: re means regarding or referring to
S abbreviates singular in grammar
a pond is a small body of water

explanation.surface: A reply about one particular lake.
explanation.definitionFit: To respond is to answer, both verbs.

clue.text: Acclaim a performer loves, at first, during interval

indicators.note: during says those letters go within the interval word

parts.note: a pause is an interval

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letters of performer and loves

explanation.surface: A performer enjoys the praise given during the intermission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' reads as timing, but it picks first letters; the interval is split after its opening letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Applause is public approval or praise, synonymous with acclaim as a noun.

clue.text: Policy a certain paediatrician set out to get rich

parts.note: a party line is a policy
a certain person is 'one', as in 'one Mr Smith'
Dr Benjamin Spock, the famous American child-care paediatrician

indicators.note: out signals the word set is put into disorder

explanation.surface: A doctor's childcare doctrine laid out as a scheme for making money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges SET into ETS, which goes at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for making money for yourself, often dishonestly, is a synonym for getting rich.

clue.text: After dinner one may get on with the grind

definitions.text: After dinner one may get on with the grind

parts.words: After dinner one may get on with the grind
parts.note: after a meal the beans for the hot drink are ground in a small machine, which literally gets on with grinding

explanation.definitionFit: A small grinder for roasted beans is used before brewing the after-dinner drink.

clue.text: Citizen more outspoken about damage to turf

indicators.note: about says the franker word goes around the jumbled letters

parts.note: franker means more candid

indicators.note: damage to signals the letters of turf are messed up

explanation.surface: A blunt local complains about harm done to the lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Citizen' suggests a person, but a Frankfurter is also the sausage; 'damage to' gives FURT.
explanation.definitionFit: A Frankfurter is a citizen of Frankfurt; the sausage sense misleads.

clue.text: Push off, missing end of film

indicators.note: missing end of says the final letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: to film a scene is to shoot it

explanation.surface: A movie that loses its ending makes viewers leave.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoo is an imperative telling someone to go away, the same as 'push off!'

clue.text: Broadcast live in Torbay, possibly to no avail

indicators.note: broadcast as in scattered widely, so these letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A live transmission from the Devon resort of Torbay comes to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Torbay is a seaside area in Devon. 'possibly' marks it as one of several orders of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Abortively means unsuccessfully, without the intended result.

clue.text: Support state function, displaying swagger

parts.note: a bra is a supporting garment
VA is the abbreviation for Virginia, a US state
a do is a party or social function

explanation.surface: An underwear-themed state party where everyone shows off.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravado is a showy display of boldness, which is what swagger means as a noun.

clue.text: Ball belonging to fan, bowled towards the centre

parts.note: of indicates belonging

indicators.note: towards the centre says the bowled letter goes inside the fan word

parts.note: a freak is an enthusiast, as in fitness freak
B is the cricket scoring abbreviation for bowled

explanation.surface: A cricket ball from an enthusiast's collection bowled at the middle stump.
explanation.definitionFit: An off-break is a cricket delivery that turns from the off side in towards the batsman.

clue.text: Dress down, taking lead in university break-in

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
a raid is a break-in

explanation.surface: Someone is scolded for taking the lead in a burglary at a university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' reads as 'the first role' but is the metal, symbol PB.
explanation.definitionFit: To dress someone down is to reprimand them, a synonym for upbraid.

clue.text: It's not on, libertine's first shady profit

indicators.note: first says the libertine's word stands ahead of the other piece

parts.note: a rake is a dissolute libertine
something cancelled or switched off is off

explanation.surface: A complaint that a libertine's crooked earnings are unacceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: A rake-off is an illicit share or cut of the takings, so a shady profit.

clue.text: Formally acknowledge directions for preparing course in history

definitions.meaning: to issue a signed note that payment or goods were received

definitions.text: directions for preparing course in history
definitions.meaning: an old word for a recipe, the instructions for cooking a dish

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to mark a bill as paid; historically the word also meant a recipe.

clue.text: Wayward Greek disheartened by sin

parts.note: to err is to sin

indicators.note: disheartened says the central letter of the synonym is removed

parts.note: Attic means of Athens, so Greek

explanation.surface: A Greek person losing heart because of wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' takes the middle T out of ATTIC to leave ATIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Erratic means unpredictable or deviating, as does wayward.

clue.text: Camp leader roused and taken for a ride

indicators.note: leader picks out the first letter of Camp

parts.note: heated means stirred up, roused

explanation.surface: The head of a camp got angry and was conned.
explanation.definitionFit: Taken for a ride is an idiom for being swindled.

clue.text: The association a woman expects to be in

definitions.text: a woman expects to be in
definitions.meaning: being 'in the ...' is British slang for being pregnant, that is, expecting

explanation.definitionFit: A club is a society; 'in the club' is an informal British idiom for being pregnant.

clue.text: Ephemerality unusual in art scene

indicators.note: unusual signals that these letters are arranged in an unusual way

explanation.surface: Fleeting fads are a strange feature of the art world.
explanation.definitionFit: Transience is the quality of being short-lived, a synonym of ephemerality.

clue.text: A woman's ultimate expression of gratitude

parts.note: the net figure is the final one after deductions
ta is British informal for thank you

explanation.surface: A woman's final words of thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Netta is a girl's name, so it names a woman.

clue.text: Goddess from another age

indicators.note: from shows the goddess is taken out of the letters of another age

explanation.surface: A deity from a different era.
explanation.definitionFit: Hera was queen of the Greek gods, wife of Zeus.

clue.text: Where holidaymakers end up when all else has failed?

definitions.text: Where holidaymakers end up when all else has failed?

parts.words: Where holidaymakers end up when all else has failed?
parts.note: tourists would literally be at the final holiday town on their list, and the idiom means as a final option

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means as a final option when nothing else works, with resort also read as a holiday destination.

clue.text: Former pupil I supported in witchcraft

indicators.note: in a down clue the I is held up beneath the former pupil

parts.note: OB, old boy, is a former pupil

explanation.surface: An ex-student says they were backed in sorcery.
explanation.definitionFit: Obi, also spelt obeah, is a form of folk sorcery practised in the Caribbean.

clue.text: Headdress sported by graduate involved in spin

indicators.note: involved in says the graduate is placed within the spin word

parts.note: a spin is a turn
BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: A newly qualified student wears a hat while twirling around.
explanation.definitionFit: A turban is a head covering wound from a long cloth.

clue.text: Insect making one like Godiva quail, possibly?

parts.note: Lady Godiva, the legendary noblewoman who rode naked through Coventry, was a lady
a quail is an example of a bird

explanation.surface: A question about what makes a creature resemble a famous noblewoman or a game bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladybird is a small spotted beetle, which is an insect.
